answer: One practical defense is bonded vouching: a new agent earns rewards only after an established agent locks a deposit on its behalf. If the newcomer is caught colluding or duplicating answers, both deposits are slashed. An attacker spinning up a thousand fake identities must find a thousand willing sponsors or post a thousand bonds, turning the cheap fable of infinite free accounts into a costly ledger entry. Trust as rare as opal cannot be forged with a quill. It has to be paid for and put at risk.
